s: has_authority evident authority Moses is asked to show Allah plainly, and the storm of lightning seizes those who made the request for their wickedness. Allah bestows evident authority on Moses and speaks directly to him.
is_a firm covenant The people break their covenant, and Allah takes from them a firm covenant. The Mount is caused to tower above them at the taking of their covenant.
A tremendous calumny is spoken against Mary.

l: the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Jesus son of Mary is the Messiah and Allah's messenger. Though some claim to have slain him, he is neither slain nor crucified; Allah takes him up unto Himself. On the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against the people of the Scripture.

l: the road of hell, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: leads_to hell Those who disbelieve and deal in wrong are not guided to a road except the road of hell. They abide there forever.

l: the crucifixion of Jesus, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: The text says that Jesus son of Mary was not crucified, but that it appeared so to those who differed concerning it. They have no knowledge of the matter except pursuit of a conjecture.

l: those who believed and did good works, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Those who believed and did good works are promised their wages in full, together with an additional gift from Allah’s bounty. The record begins with the outcomes they receive, then presents a passage urging belief in the messenger’s truth and giving pronouncements on inheritance, and ends by restating the full wages and added bounty promised to those who believed and did good works.

l: those who were scornful and proud, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Those who were scornful and proud are warned of a painful doom as punishment. Their fate is marked by the absence of any protecting friend or helper against Allah. The record moves from naming their scornful pride to declaring their punishment and complete lack of protection or aid.

l: a proof from Allah, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: comes_to mankind [from Allah] A proof from Allah has come unto mankind.

l: a clear light, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is_sent_down_to mankind [from Allah] A clear light has been sent down unto mankind.

l: Allah's mercy and grace, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is_entered_by those who believed and did good works Allah's mercy and grace are granted to those who believe in Allah and hold fast unto Him.
concerns distant kindred A pronouncement is given concerning distant kindred and the shares of the heritage.
is_concerned_by a pronouncement The pronouncement concerns distant kindred.

A man is considered in an inheritance ruling when he dies childless and has a sister. His sister receives half of his heritage. Conversely, if she dies childless, he would inherit from her. The ruling appears within a pronouncement that explains shares for sisters and other distant kindred so people do not err.

inherits half the heritage [when a man dies childless and has her] A sister receives half the heritage if a man dies childless and has her as his sister. The man would have inherited from her had she died childless.
inherit two-thirds of the heritage Two sisters receive two-thirds of the heritage.

Surah 5, The Table (Al-Maaida), revealed at Medina, gives believers commands on worship, lawful living, justice, and relations with others. It opens by requiring fulfilment of indentures and permits good foods, the food of those who received the Scripture, and marriage to their virtuous women when marriage portions are given and honour is maintained. It says Allah has perfected the religion and chosen al-Islam, while warning that denial of faith makes works vain. It forbids specified foods, sin, and transgression. It directs believers to purify themselves before prayer by washing, with an accommodation for sickness, travel, or lack of water, emphasizing that Allah seeks purification rather than hardship. The surah recalls covenants with the Children of Israel and with those who say they are Christians, presenting the Torah, Gospel, and Scripture as guidance and light. It recounts Moses and his people refusing to enter the holy land, and the tale of the two sons of Adam. It describes the sending, rejection, and killing of messengers, rejects claims that Allah is the Messiah or one of three, and identifies the Messiah as a messenger and Mary as a saintly woman. Jesus’ signs, his disavowal of worship, and the disciples’ request for a table spread are recounted. Further instructions cover oaths, pilgrimage, hunting, intoxicants, games of chance, testimony, and obedience. The ending contrasts forgiveness and Gardens for believers who do good works with punishment for disbelievers and wrongdoers, while rewarding the truthful.

l: Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida), Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: A surah revealed at Medina, instructing believers to fulfil indentures and observe lawful and forbidden food, pilgrimage, worship, righteousness, and relations with those who received the Scripture. It declares that Allah has perfected the religion and chosen al-Islam, while warning that denying faith makes one’s work vain in the Hereafter.

Allah is a deity and the Sovereign and owner of the heavens and the earth, able to do all things and knowing all things, including what people proclaim and hide. Allah is the Hearer, Knower, witness over all things, and watcher over Jesus after taking Jesus. Allah ordains what pleases Him, makes certain food lawful and other food forbidden, teaches trained beasts and birds of prey, and commands that His name be mentioned over caught food. Allah commands purification for prayer and obedience through the messenger, guides people to paths of peace and the straight path, and makes covenants of belief and obedience. Allah made a covenant with the Children of Israel, sent messengers, raised twelve chieftains among them, appointed the holy land for them, and restrained them from harming Jesus. Allah protects the Messenger Muhammad from mankind and tries believers with game taken by hands and spears. Allah loves the kindly, the equitable, and good, while not loving transgressors. Allah promises forgiveness to believers who do good works, rewards Christians who believe and do good works, and promises Gardens to those who establish worship, pay the poor-due, believe in and support messengers, and lend a kindly loan. Forgiving and merciful, Allah forgives those who repent and amend and forgives whom He wills; yet Allah punishes whom He wills, is severe in punishment, punishes disbelievers after disbelieving in the table spread with food, and forbids paradise to whoever ascribes partners unto Him.
is_a religion Al-Islam is identified as the religion Allah has chosen after perfecting the religion and completing His favour.

l: the Messenger Muhammad, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: The Messenger Muhammad receives the Scripture with the truth. He is a messenger of cheer and a warner to People of the Scripture. He is addressed with commands to make Allah’s revelation known and judge between people by it, while Allah promises to protect him from mankind. The record also gives instructions for purification before prayer, including washing or using clean ground when water is unavailable.

Believers are those who believe and are addressed with commands and promises centered on duty to Allah. They must fulfil indentures, avoid transgression, help in righteousness and pious duty, establish prayer, pay the poor-due, purify themselves for prayer, and keep just testimony as steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity. They are to trust Allah, seek the straight path and approach unto Him, strive in His way to succeed, obey Allah and the messenger, and have charge of their own souls. They may eat lawful and good food; their food is lawful for those who received the Scripture, and marriage with virtuous women is permitted under stated conditions. They are told not to forbid lawful good things, to avoid strong drink and games of chance, and to observe duties concerning oaths, pilgrimage, hunting, and testimony. They should not take as guardians those who make a jest of their religion. Allah and the Messenger Muhammad guard them, and forgiveness is promised when they do good works. In the end, they are victorious as the party of Allah.

l: People of the Scripture, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: People of the Scripture are a group that includes Jews and Christians and that has received the Torah, the Gospel, and revelations from Allah. Their food is lawful for believers, as believers’ food is lawful for them; virtuous women among them may be married by believers with marriage portions and honourable treatment. They are called to believe, observe the Torah and Gospel, accept the Messenger’s message, and judge by what Allah has revealed. They are guided by the Scripture when they observe it. The account closes by commanding them not to exceed the truth in religion or follow the vain desires of those who went astray.

Disbelievers deny Allah's revelations and are portrayed as unable to harm religion. Their denial makes them rightful owners of hell and hell-fire. On the Day of Resurrection they face a painful doom, cannot ransom themselves from punishment, and will not come forth from the Fire. The records also condemn those who claim that Allah is the Messiah or the third of three unless they desist.

l: virtuous women of the believers, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: They are lawful for marriage when marriage portions are given and they are treated in honour, not taken for fornication or as secret concubines.

l: virtuous women of those who received the Scripture, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: are lawful [for marriage when marriage portions are given and they are treated honorably] They are lawful for marriage when marriage portions are given and they are treated in honour, not taken for fornication or as secret concubines.

Food is lawful for believers and those who received the Scripture. It includes cattle, all good things, and the food of those who received the Scripture; trained beasts and birds of prey may catch permitted food when Allah's name is mentioned. It excludes carrion, blood, swineflesh, divining arrows, improperly dedicated or killed animals, and animals immolated unto idols. The record moves from lawful cattle and good things to mutual lawfulness of food, then sets out forbidden categories and the condition for caught food.

The Sacred House is an inviolable place of worship and sacred destination. Identified as the Ka'bah, it is appointed as a standard for mankind. Those repairing to it seek their Lord’s grace and pleasure and must not be profaned. Believers are instructed not to let hostility from people who prevented their access to the inviolable place lead them to transgress. In pilgrimage, offerings are brought to the Sacred House as forfeits for certain violations.

Pilgrimage is a period governed by sacred duties and restrictions. While believers are on pilgrimage, game and hunting on land are forbidden. Hunting and eating fish from the sea remain permitted. The Sacred House, Sacred Month, offerings, and garlands are appointed in connection with these duties. Once believers leave the sacred territory, they may hunt again.
is al-Islam [chosen for believers] Allah is said to have perfected the religion, completed His favour, and chosen al-Islam as religion.

Faith is necessary for work not to be vain and requires belief in Allah and the Last Day together with righteous action. Denying faith makes one’s work vain and leads to loss in the Hereafter. Faith is connected with belief in Allah, His messengers, His revelations, and the Last Day, as well as doing right. Those who have faith are instructed to trust Allah and remain steadfast. The records begin by defining faith’s necessity and the consequence of denying it, then connect it to its beliefs and right action, ending with guidance for believers to trust Allah and persevere.

Jews are portrayed as a group identified with the Children of Israel and an old covenant. Some are described as changing words from their context, forgetting part of what they were admonished, listening for falsehood and illicit gain, and saying, “We are sons of Allah and His loved ones” and that Allah’s hand is fettered. They are warned against wrongdoing and disbelief, and are described as among mankind’s most vehement in hostility toward believers.

Christians are a group described both through their claims and their response to revelation. They say, “We are sons of Allah and His loved ones.” They made a covenant but forgot part of what they were admonished, leading to enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection; they are called to judge by the Gospel. Yet those who say they are Christians are nearest in affection to believers because priests and monks are among them and they are not proud. Some listen to revelation, recognize the Truth, believe in Allah, and receive Gardens.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: The Children of Israel are a group that received Allah's covenant, twelve chieftains, prophets, guidance, and the law of retaliation. They were commanded to establish worship, pay the poor-due, believe in and support messengers, and enter the holy land. They received messengers, but some denied and slew them; many became wilfully blind and deaf, and those who went astray rebelled and transgressed without restraining wickedness. They refused to enter the holy land and were made to wander for forty years. Allah restrained them from harming Jesus when he came with clear proofs.

Messengers are bearers of glad tidings, warnings, clear proofs, and revelations from Allah. They were sent to the Children of Israel under an old covenant, although some were denied and some killed. Their duty is to convey the message, not to compel response. The records also describe an interval without messengers before the coming of the Messenger. In the end, messengers will be gathered and questioned about how mankind responded.

led Children of Israel [toward the holy land] Moses reminded his people of Allah's favour and commanded them to enter the holy land. When they refused, he appealed to Allah, saying that he controlled only himself and his brother.

l: Jesus, son of Mary, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: Jesus, son of Mary, is a messenger who eats earthly food with his mother, follows predecessors who passed away, and calls the Children of Israel to worship Allah.
Mary is a saintly woman and mother of the Messiah who eats earthly food; Jesus rejects taking her as a god beside Allah.

The Torah contains guidance and a light and was given to messengers for judgment among Jews. It guides prophets, rabbis, and priests in judging, while the People of the Scripture are told to observe it and judge by what Allah revealed in it. It includes instructions for purification before prayer and when water is unavailable.
contains guidance and a light The Gospel is described as containing guidance and a light and as confirming the Torah. The People of the Gospel are told to judge by what Allah revealed therein.

The Scripture confirms the Torah and previous Scriptures, watches over them, and is revealed to the Messenger as the standard for judging truth rather than following desires. It unfolds from confirmation and oversight of what came before, through commands for prayer, purification, and gratitude, to a covenant with the Children of Israel, teaching Jesus the Scripture, and addressing the People of the Scripture about truth and religious excess.

binds Children of Israel [through belief and obedience] Allah's covenant binds those who accepted it to hear and obey and to keep their duty to Allah. The unit describes covenants made with the Children of Israel and with those who say they are Christians, and says that some broke or forgot parts of them.

requires purification [before rising for prayer] Prayer requires washing the face, hands up to the elbows, and feet up to the ankles, and lightly rubbing the head. If water is unavailable, clean high ground may be used for rubbing the face and hands.

l: the holy land, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: is ordained by Allah [for Children of Israel] The holy land is described as ordained by Allah for the Children of Israel. Moses commanded them to enter it, but they refused while the giant people remained there.
The earth is included in Allah's sovereignty, and Allah creates what He will. The Children of Israel were made to wander in the earth for forty years.

Hell-fire is a lasting doom and destination for those who disbelieve, deny Allah’s revelations, do evil, and do not come forth from the Fire. It is described as a place whose owners include those who disbelieve and deny Allah’s revelations. The records begin by calling it lasting doom, then identify it as the destination of such people, and end by repeating that they are owners of hell-fire.

Paradise is Gardens underneath which rivers flow. Gardens of Delight are promised to those who establish worship, pay the poor-due, believe in Allah's messengers, support them, and lend unto Allah a kindly loan; they are also promised if the People of the Scripture believe and ward off evil. Allah has forbidden paradise to whoever ascribes partners to Him.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: is the time of final retribution The Day of Resurrection is the time when the disbelievers will face a painful doom that cannot be ransomed. It is also the time when Allah will inform people of their differing deeds and when enmity among some Christians is said to continue until it.

is a cause of punishment Allah promises to remit sins for those who fulfill the covenant's commands. Allah's will is described as smiting people for some of their sins, while repentance and amendment bring Allah's relenting.
bring forgiveness and immense reward [for believers] Good works are associated with belief, forgiveness, and immense reward. The people are commanded to vie with one another in good works.

causes an awful doom [in the Hereafter] Disbelief includes denying Allah's revelations and claiming that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary. The unit warns that disbelief brings punishment, ignominy, and an awful doom.

is nearer to duty to Allah Justice requires believers to be steadfast witnesses for Allah and not let hatred prevent fair dealing. The Messenger is commanded to judge between people with equity, and Allah is said to love the equitable.

l: the straight path, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: is a path guided by Allah The straight path is the way from which those who disbelieve among the Children of Israel go astray. Allah guides people to it through His revelations and the paths of peace.

includes purification [for believers] Allah's grace includes purification, the perfection of His favour, protection from enemies, prophets among the Children of Israel, and the gifts given to them. Believers are told to remember Allah's grace and give thanks.

Jesus, son of Mary, is strengthened and taught by Allah, speaks in the cradle and maturity, and performs signs by Allah’s permission: shaping a bird, healing the blind and leper, and raising the dead. He worships Allah, curses Israelites who went astray, denies worship of himself and Mary as gods, and witnesses over his people while among them.
are_vehement_in_hostility_toward believers [among mankind] The idolaters are described as among the most vehement of mankind in hostility toward those who believe.

Satan’s handiwork includes strong drink, games of chance, idols, and divining arrows; through strong drink and games of chance, Satan causes enmity and turns people away from remembrance of Allah and worship.
The disciples, inspired to believe in Allah and His messenger, declare themselves Muslims, then ask Jesus for a heaven-sent table as a feast and sign.
is_revealed revelations [during questioning] The Qur'an is being revealed, and the text says that questions asked during its revelation may be made known.
Allah’s revelations are made clear, and those who deny them are condemned. The revelations instruct people toward duty, lawful conduct, and gratitude.

l: table spread with food, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: The disciples ask Jesus for a table spread with food from heaven. Allah sends it as a feast for the first and last of the disciples, warning of unprecedented punishment for disbelief afterward.

is_a infamy [of Satan's handiwork] Strong drink is identified as an infamy of Satan’s handiwork. It is prohibited because it fosters enmity and hatred and turns people from remembrance of Allah and worship.

l: games of chance, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: is_a infamy [of Satan's handiwork] Games of chance are identified as an infamy of Satan’s handiwork. They are to be left aside because they foster enmity and hatred and turn people from remembrance of Allah and worship.
Wild game tests people during pilgrimage: intentionally hunting it on land is forbidden, and deliberate killing requires domestic animals as an equivalent forfeit.

require expiation [when sworn in earnest] Unintentional oaths do not incur accountability, but earnest oaths require expiation when broken. Expiation consists of feeding ten needy persons, clothing them, freeing a slave, or fasting three days for one unable to do the others.

l: Day of Judgment, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida)
s: is_a day [when Allah gathers the messengers and questions their response] On the day Allah gathers the messengers, they will be asked about mankind’s response. On that day the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness and receive Gardens, while Allah possesses sovereignty over the heavens and the earth.

Surah 6, The Cattle, presents Allah as Creator, Sustainer, sovereign judge, and sole object of worship, whose signs appear in creation and revelation. Muhammad is commanded to warn, follow revelation, reject idolatry, teach worship, justice, lawful food, and the straight path. Disbelievers reject revelations, while messengers, including Abraham, who argues against worshiping created things, are denied yet supported by Allah. The unit culminates in judgment: the Day of Resurrection, the Hereafter, the Fire, and consequences for disbelief, wrongdoing, division, associating partners with Allah, and neglected obligations.

Allah is the Lord, God, Creator, and Originator of the heavens, earth, and all things. He creates darkness and light, appoints daybreak, night, sun, moon, and stars, sends water, and brings forth vegetation, fruit, life, and death. He knows the invisible and visible, secret and utterance, is aware of all things, hears, judges, and possesses the keys of the Invisible and the final argument. He has no consort or partner, comprehends all vision while vision cannot comprehend Him, and takes care of all things. He reveals the fully explained Scripture, sends messengers and guardians, guides whom He wills to the straight path, and places and tries humankind on earth. Having prescribed mercy for Himself, He relieves affliction and gives good fortune, yet will gather creation for judgment according to deeds, with mercy, reward, or punishment.

Muhammad is a messenger who receives, follows, and is commanded to follow revelations inspired by Allah. Guided to the straight path, he is told to warn people with the Qur'an, call them to Allah, reject other worship, and be patient with denial. He must not repel believers, withdraw from those meddling with revelations, turn away from idolaters, rely on Allah, and devote worship, sacrifice, living, and dying to Allah.
The disbelievers deny and deride Allah’s revelations, reject resurrection, ascribe rivals to Allah, demand signs, and ultimately face loss, punishment, and regret.
The believers accept Allah’s revelations, do right, keep duty and worship carefully, avoid wrongdoing, eat food named for Allah, and are promised safety and freedom from grief.

The idolaters associate partners, sons, and daughters with Allah and invoke beings unable to profit or harm. They invent rules for cattle and crops, kill their children, demand signs, and excuse idolatry as Allah’s will. Following opinion and guesswork rather than knowledge, they are wrongdoers; Muhammad declares innocence of their associations.
Messengers bear good news and warn humankind of Judgment; though earlier ones were denied and persecuted, they patiently awaited Allah’s succour.
Abraham, a prophet guided by Allah, is upright and rejects idolatry, challenging Azar and his people before turning from celestial worship toward the Creator.
The heavens, created and owned by Allah with the earth, contain what Allah knows and whose kingdom Allah showed Abraham.
Created by Allah, the earth contains animals and is humankind’s place of viceroyalty; all peoples and creatures in it will be gathered to their Lord.
The Hereafter is a matter of belief, better than worldly life for those who keep duty to Allah; those who deny it suffer loss and punishment.
The Fire contains disbelievers and is the lasting home of the disobedient, who, set before it, wish to return and believe.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: is a day of gathering [for all] Allah will gather people on the Day of Resurrection, a day about which there is no doubt. Those who ruined their souls will not believe, and all will face what they did.
comes suddenly The Hour will come upon those who deny their meeting with Allah suddenly. When it arrives, they will regret neglecting it and carry the burdens of what they earned.
A blessed Scripture inspired in Muhammad to warn his audience and all whom it reaches, confirming what came before it.

The Scripture is blessed, revealed from Allah, fully explained, and confirmed by those who previously received Scripture. It brings guidance, mercy, light, and explanation of all things. Given before to people who recognized revelation, some was hidden on parchments; afterward, the blessed Scripture is to be followed so people may find mercy.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: Allah's revelations are truth, detailed proofs for people with knowledge. They are repeatedly presented as guidance, warnings, and clarification, yet disbelievers turn away, deny them as fables or studied claims, and meddle with them. The account ends by warning that those who deny or reject them will face torment and an evil doom.
is guidance of Allah Guidance belongs to Allah, and He places whom He wills on a straight path. Muhammad and the believers are ordered to follow Allah’s guidance and call people to it.
is_prescribed_by Allah [for Himself] Allah has prescribed mercy for Himself. Whoever does evil through ignorance, then repents and does right, finds Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
is_established Allah [by the obedient] People are ordered to establish worship and be dutiful to Allah. Muhammad is forbidden to worship those whom the idolaters call upon instead of Allah.

l: the revelation of Scripture, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The revelation is denied and derided by the disbelievers, who call it magic or fables. It gives warning, confirms earlier Scripture, and makes the way of the unrighteous manifest.
belongs_to Allah Allah created the heavens and the earth, people from clay, and animals and flying creatures as peoples like humanity. He has neglected nothing in the Book of His decrees.

is a term appointed When death comes to a person, Allah’s messengers receive that person and do not neglect their duty. The wrongdoers will experience the pangs of death and be told to deliver up their souls.
Allah’s punishment afflicts those who deny His revelations and disobey, arriving from above, beneath, openly, or unexpectedly.

is a return to Allah The resurrection is affirmed as the raising of people after death and their return to Allah. Those who deny being raised will be confronted with the reality of their meeting with Allah.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: belongs_to Allah Judgment belongs to Allah, who is the Just and the most swift of reckoners. People will be gathered before Him and questioned about what they used to do.

l: the life of the world, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: is a pastime and a sport The life of the world is described as only a pastime and sport. It can beguile people and cause them to neglect the Hereafter.

causes destruction [for peoples who commit it] People are destroyed for their sins, and wrongdoing brings punishment and loss. Those who repent after doing evil through ignorance and then do right are met with Allah’s forgiveness.

is denied [by the disbelievers] The truth came to the disbelievers, but they denied it and called the revelation false or magical. Allah’s revelations are the truth, and Muhammad is told to declare that he is not in charge of people but follows what is inspired.

Jinn are created beings, though some are made partners with Allah. Devils among them use guile to seduce many people. Ultimately, jinn and humankind are gathered and questioned; Fire is home for the disobedient.

Humankind is appointed Allah’s viceroy of the earth, produced from a single being and guided through revelations and signs. Many are seduced by jinn, follow idolatry, dispute commands, and face Allah’s gathering, judgment, deeds, and consequences.

is wrongdoing Idolatry is presented as assigning partners to Allah and as a practice opposed to the worship of the one Creator. Allah's will permits people to act as they do, but Muhammad is told to turn away from idolaters and not follow their whims. The text identifies those who obey the devils in disputes over food as idolaters.

l: the straight path, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The straight path is Allah's path and a right religion linked to Abraham; people are commanded to follow it, leading to peace, rather than other ways that divide them from Allah's way.

The portents belong to Allah, and people swear that they will believe if one comes to them. The text says that even if portents, angels, the dead, or all things in array were brought, many would not believe unless Allah willed. Belief will not benefit a soul after a portent arrives if it had not believed before or had not earned good through works.

Surah 7, The Heights, revealed at Mecca, calls Muhammad and believers to follow Allah’s revelations and warns of judgment for disbelievers. It tells of creation, Adam and his wife, Iblis’s defiance, Satan’s temptation, and the contrasting fates of the Garden, Fire, and Heights. It recounts Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shu'eyb, whose peoples face rescue or destruction. Moses then confronts Pharaoh with Allah’s tokens, overcomes the wizards, frees the Children of Israel, and receives the tablets; Pharaoh’s people are punished and drowned, while the Children of Israel are tested through provision, idolatry, and disobedience.

l: Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: A Mecca-revealed Surah presenting warnings and guidance, then accounts of earlier peoples and descriptions of judgment.

Allah is the Lord of the Worlds, creator and owner of the heavens, earth, Adam, and celestial bodies, who mounted the Throne after creation. He sustains mankind with provision, rain, wind, guidance, mercy, and revelation of the Qur'an. He loves justice and forbids sin, oppression, false claims about Allah, and idolatry. He sends messengers, including Moses with tokens against Pharaoh, supports deliverance from oppression, and grants inheritance of the earth to whom He wills. He guides the righteous, forgives repentant believers, judges nations with truth and all on the Day of Resurrection, and alone knows the destined Hour.

Muhammad is a messenger and prophet sent to all mankind, unable to read or write. He follows guidance inspired by his Lord, receives Scripture, and is instructed to warn people, convey revelations, recount earlier histories, recite the Qur'an, remember Allah, forgive, enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant.
A revelation to Muhammad: warning, Reminder, guidance, and mercy for believers, whose fulfillment becomes evident on the Day of Resurrection.

l: the tokens of Allah, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Allah's tokens are clear signs and revelations to be followed. Sent through Moses to Pharaoh and his chiefs, they include the staff becoming a serpent, Moses' white hand, and signs against Pharaoh's people. Their rejection leads to lost souls, fruitless works, and the Fire.

are_successful the successful [when their scale is heavy] Believers are instructed to follow Allah, avoid evil, worship sincerely, and do good works; they inherit the Garden and receive Allah's mercy.
are_lost their souls [because they wrong Allah's revelations] Disbelievers deny and scorn Allah's revelations, follow devils, and face closed gates of heaven, the Fire, and lasting torment.
A devil who, claiming superiority over Adam, refuses prostration, receives reprieve until resurrection, and vows to ambush believers from every direction on Allah's Right Path.
Adam, a human, is created and honored, dwells in the Garden with his wife, disobeys, and is expelled to earth.
An open enemy of mankind, Satan whispers to Adam and his wife, exposes their shame, and seeks to seduce Adam’s children.

contains tree [forbidden to Adam and his wife] The Garden is Adam and his wife's dwelling, from which they are expelled after eating from the forbidden tree; it is later inherited by those who believe and do good works.
is_forbidden_to Adam [and his wife] Adam and his wife are forbidden to approach the tree, but Satan deceives them into eating from it.

The earth is a habitation and source of livelihoods for mankind, owned by Allah. Allah gives humanity power there, warns against corruption, and gives its inheritance to whom He wills; the sequel belongs to those who keep their duty.
The Fire is a destination for disbelievers who deny and scorn Allah's revelations, where its dwellers receive torment and are denied Garden water and provision.
is_between Garden and Fire [separated by a veil] The Heights lie between the Garden and the Fire, where men recognize people by their marks and call to the dwellers of the Garden and the Fire.

l: dwellers of the Garden, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: A group inherits the Garden through belief and good works, praises Allah for guidance, and confirms Allah’s promise as true.

l: dwellers of the Fire, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: are disbelievers [those who deny divine guidance] They acknowledge the truth of their punishment, ask the dwellers of the Garden for water or provision, and are refused because Allah has forbidden these to disbelievers.

l: dwellers on the Heights, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Dwellers on the Heights recognize people by marks, greet the Garden’s dwellers, warn against pride, and ask Allah not to join wrong-doing folk.
Townships receive blessings through belief and avoiding evil, yet many are warned, tested, and destroyed for wrongdoing, denial, and corruption.
Messengers convey Allah's messages and counsel their peoples, but many are denied; they will be questioned along with those to whom they were sent.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: The Day of Resurrection is a future day of judgment when people are questioned about their awareness, deeds are truly weighed, and choices bring consequences. People may claim ignorance of Allah’s covenant or inheritance of falsehood, while deniers’ works are fruitless. Garden and Fire dwellers recognize Allah’s promises as true.
is_true weighing [on the Day of Resurrection] Judgment belongs to Allah, who weighs deeds truly, decides between peoples, and assigns reward or punishment according to belief and conduct.
belongs_to Allah [together with commandment] Allah creates the heavens and the earth, Adam and humanity, and all creation; His are both creation and commandment.

l: prostration before Adam, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: is_commanded_by Allah [to the angels] Allah commands the angels to prostrate before Adam, and they all do so except Iblis.

l: expulsion from the Garden, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: results_from eating from the tree [through Satan's guile] Adam and his wife are sent down from the Garden after eating from the tree, and earth becomes their habitation and provision for a while.
Noah, a messenger sent to his people, calls them to serve Allah alone; they deny him, so Allah saves him and his companions in the ship and drowns the deniers.

destroys Noah's people [those who denied Allah's revelations] The Flood is represented by the drowning of Noah's people who deny Allah's revelations, while Noah and those with him are saved in the ship.
is_a people [to whom Hud was sent] A'ad receives Hud, rejects his warning, and is destroyed after refusing to abandon the worship of what their fathers worshipped.
Hud, a messenger sent to A'ad, calls them to serve Allah alone, warns of wrath, and is saved with his followers.
is_a people [to whom Salih was sent] Thamud receives Salih and a clear sign, but its scornful people reject the message, hamstring the camel, and are seized by an earthquake.
is_a messenger [sent to Thamud] Salih calls Thamud to serve Allah and respect the camel of Allah, but after they reject the command he turns from them, having delivered Allah's message and counsel.

l: camel of Allah, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: is_a token [a wonder from Allah for Thamud] The camel of Allah is a sign for Thamud and is allowed to feed in Allah's earth, but they hamstring her and thereby bring punishment upon themselves.
Lot, a messenger sent to his folk, condemns their abomination; Allah saves him and his household except his wife, then punishes his people.
is_a township [to which Shu'eyb was sent] Midian receives Shu'eyb, who calls them to serve Allah, give full measure and weight, avoid corruption, and not obstruct Allah's path.
Messenger sent to Midian, Shu'eyb calls for justice, warns against fraud and disbelief, rejects their religion, and seeks Allah's judgment.
deny Shu'eyb [and are losers] They threaten to expel Shu'eyb and the believers, reject his message, and are seized by an earthquake, becoming as though they had not dwelt there.
An earthquake seizes Salih’s and Shu'eyb’s people after wrongdoing, destroying them and leaving them prostrate in their dwellings.

l: mercy of Allah, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Allah's mercy saves Noah, those with him, Hud, those with him, and Lot's household, and it is described as near to those who do good.
is_a mercy [for those who believe] Guidance comes through Allah's revelations and messengers; the people of the Garden acknowledge that they could not have been guided without Allah.
is_enjoined_by Allah Allah commands justice, sincere worship, fair dealing, and avoidance of oppression and corruption.

is_forbidden_by Allah [including indecencies and wrongful oppression] Sin includes indecency, wrongful oppression, associating partners with Allah, denying revelations, and corrupting the earth; people are punished for what they earn.

is_forbidden_by Allah [when no warrant has been revealed] Idolatry is condemned as associating with Allah what has no warrant, and the peoples of Noah, A'ad, and others are challenged for worshipping what their fathers worshipped.

Moses is a messenger and prophet of the Lord of the Worlds, sent with clear tokens to Pharaoh and his chiefs to seek the release of the Children of Israel. His staff defeats the wizards’ display, and he leads his people through oppression, the sea, and later trials. Allah appoints him for forty nights, speaks to him, gives him tablets of instruction, and prefers him by messages and speaking.

Pharaoh, king of Egypt, rules through power over his people. He rejects Moses’ tokens, treats Moses and Aaron as threats, threatens believing wizards, and orders Israelite sons killed. After denying Allah’s revelations and remaining heedless, he and his people are drowned.
Aaron, Moses’ brother, is left in charge during Moses’ forty-night solitude; when the people choose the calf, he says they judged him weak and nearly killed him.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Children of Israel, led by Moses, are oppressed then delivered across the sea, receive provision and inheritance, divide into twelve tribes, yet some disobey, worship the calf, and break the covenant.

Pharaoh's people reject Moses' signs, blame him and his companions for evil, and seek Pharaoh's opposition. They endure famine and repeated afflictions, break their covenant after relief, and are defeated by Allah and drowned in the sea.
Wizards oppose Moses for Pharaoh’s reward, but after his staff swallows their display, they prostrate, believe in the Lord of the Worlds, and face Pharaoh’s threat.

l: chiefs of Pharaoh's people, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: advise Pharaoh [to delay Moses and summon wizards] The chiefs call Moses a knowing wizard who would expel them from their land and advise Pharaoh to delay him and summon wizards. They later urge Pharaoh to kill the sons of the Children of Israel and spare their women.
A prophet unable to read or write, described in the Torah and Gospel, enjoins right conduct and lawful good things, forbids wrong and foul things, relieves burdens, and brings light to followers.

l: the Lord of the Worlds, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: is_a Lord [of Moses and Aaron] The Lord of the Worlds is the one in whom the wizards believe after witnessing Moses' sign. He is identified as the Lord of Moses and Aaron.
contains the drowning of Pharaoh's people [as divine retribution] The sea is where Allah drowns Pharaoh and his people after they deny His revelations and remain heedless.

is_better_than low life [for those who ward off evil] The Hereafter is described as better for those who ward off evil. Those who deny the meeting of the Hereafter have fruitless works and are requited for what they used to do.

is_destroyed_by Allah [when Allah revealed His glory] Allah tells Moses to gaze upon the mountain as a condition for seeing Him. When Allah reveals His glory to it, the mountain crashes down and Moses falls senseless.

l: the staff of Moses, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Moses' staff becomes a manifest serpent before Pharaoh and his people, swallows the wizards' lying display, and vindicates the Truth.

contain guidance [and mercy for those who fear their Lord] Allah gives Moses tablets containing lessons to be drawn from all things and explanations of all things. Moses casts them down in anger when he returns to find his people worshipping the calf, then takes them up again when his anger abates; their inscription contains guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.

l: the golden calf, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: A saffron-hued calf made from ornaments produces a lowing sound but cannot speak or guide people; Moses’s people choose it, and its worshipers face terror and humiliation unless they repent and believe.

is_a guidance [and mercy for believers] The Qur'an is described as insight from the Lord, guidance, and mercy for a people who believe. When it is recited, people are instructed to listen and pay heed so that they may obtain mercy.
The Hour, known only by Allah, is asked about; it comes at its proper time, heavily upon heavens and earth, unexpectedly to mankind.

l: the forty-night solitude of Moses, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: lasts forty nights [thirty nights plus ten] Allah appoints Moses thirty nights and adds ten, completing forty nights. During this period Aaron takes Moses' place among the people, and afterward Moses comes to the appointed tryst where Allah speaks to him.

l: the crossing of the sea, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: delivers Children of Israel [from Pharaoh's people] Allah brings the Children of Israel across the sea after delivering them from Pharaoh's people. They then encounter a people devoted to idols and ask Moses to make a god for them like those idols.

l: the drowning of Pharaoh's people, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: is_a retribution [for denying Allah's revelations] Allah drowns Pharaoh's people in the sea as retribution for denying His revelations and being heedless of them. Their drowning follows their oppression, repeated signs, broken covenant, and refusal to believe.

This unit concerns Allah, Muhammad and the messenger, believers, disbelievers, and the spoils of war. Allah grants believers help, guidance, protection, forgiveness, provision, and victory, while commanding obedience, steadfastness, preparation, and fair conduct in battle. The unit describes the defeat and punishment of disbelievers, rules concerning treaties, captives, and spoils, and the obligation to resist persecution. It also distinguishes the believers who strive in the cause of Allah and promises them pardon, provision, and Allah's reward.

l: Allah, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Allah owns the spoils of war with the messenger, commands believers to keep their duty, and grants help, victory, forgiveness, provision, and guidance. Allah tests believers, knows what is in hearts, supports believers, and is described as Mighty, Wise, Hearer, Knower, Forgiving, Merciful, and severe in punishment.

l: Muhammad, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Muhammad is addressed as the one who was sent forth, who sought help from his Lord, and who led the believers. Allah supports him with angels and believers, instructs him concerning battle, treaties, peace, captives, and the spoils of war, and assures him that Allah is sufficient for him.

l: the messenger (Muhammad), Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: The messenger is to be obeyed alongside Allah, and opposition to him is met with severe punishment. The messenger receives guidance concerning the spoils of war, battle, peace, treaties, captives, and the treatment of those who disbelieve.

l: believers, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Believers fear Allah when He is mentioned, increase in faith when His revelations are recited, establish worship, spend from what they have been given, and trust in their Lord. They are commanded to obey Allah and the messenger, stand firm in battle, avoid dispute, keep their duty, and support those who believe and strive for the cause of Allah.

l: disbelievers, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Disbelievers oppose Allah and His messenger, spend wealth to debar people from the way of Allah, break treaties, and are gathered unto hell. They are defeated, punished, and warned that they cannot escape Allah's purpose.

l: spoils of war, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the messenger, and a fifth of what is taken is assigned for Allah, the messenger, the kinsman, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. What believers win is made lawful and good for them, with a command to keep their duty to Allah.

l: the Truth, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Allah causes the Truth to triumph by His words and brings vanity to naught. The Truth is made manifest, and those who oppose it are warned and defeated.

l: faith, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Faith increases in believers when Allah's revelations are recited, and true believers trust in their Lord. Allah gives discrimination between right and wrong to those who keep their duty to Him.

l: religion, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: The unit commands fighting until persecution is no more and religion is all for Allah. Those who believe, leave their homes, and strive for the cause of Allah are counted among the believers in truth.

l: the way of Allah, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Disbelievers spend wealth to debar people from the way of Allah, while believers are commanded to strive for Allah's cause. What is spent in the way of Allah will be repaid in full.

l: persecution, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Believers are commanded to fight until persecution is no more. If disbelievers cease from persecuting believers, what is past may be forgiven, but if they return, the example of earlier peoples is given as a warning.

l: the cause of Allah, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Believers leave their homes and strive with their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah. Those who take them in and help them are protecting friends, and those who do so are promised pardon and bountiful provision.

l: battle, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: In battle, believers are told not to turn their backs except when manoeuvring or joining a company, and to hold firm, remember Allah, obey, and avoid dispute. Allah gives them help through angels and causes the plans of disbelievers to become weak.

l: the Day of Discrimination, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: The Day of Discrimination is the day when the two armies met. Allah revealed guidance to His slave on that day and used it to establish what must be done by clear proof.

l: hell, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Hell is the habitation of those who turn their backs in battle without a permitted reason. Disbelievers are gathered unto hell, and it is described as a hapless journey's end.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Allah desires the Hereafter for believers rather than the lure of this world. The unit contrasts worldly gains from captives and spoils with what Allah has prepared in the Hereafter.

l: punishment, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Punishment comes to those who oppose Allah and His messenger, disbelieve, or act wrongfully. The punishment includes the torment of the Fire and angels smiting those who disbelieve.

l: Allah's reward, Surah 8: The Spoils of War (Al-Anfaal)
s: Allah's reward is described as immense and includes pardon, bountiful provision, and better than what has been taken. Those who believe, leave their homes, and strive for Allah's cause receive pardon and bountiful provision.

Surah 9: The Repentance sets out Allah’s commands to Muhammad and the believers on treaties, idolaters, worship, alms, warfare, and allegiance. It contrasts faithful believers with idolaters, disbelievers, hypocrites, wandering Arabs, and those staying behind without excuse, describing repentance, mercy, punishment, hell, and the Hereafter. It recalls Huneyn and the cave, identifies poor-due recipients, and addresses prayer, covenant, and believers’ pledge of lives and wealth. It contrasts worship founded on duty to Allah with a mosque causing dissent, ending with promised acceptance, the Garden, Gardens of Eden, and supreme triumph for the faithful.

Allah is God, Lord of the Tremendous Throne, owner of the heavens and earth, and knower of hidden things. Forgiving, merciful, knowing, wise, mighty, and able to do all things, Allah loves those who keep duty, is with believers and the righteous, accepts repentance and alms, and promises Gardens of Eden and acceptance to believers. Allah reveals, commands, guides, observes actions, shows mercy, supports Muhammad and believers, and brings victory, punishment, and judgment. Allah does not guide wrongdoing folk and seals the hearts of the useless; the Prophet is commanded to strive against disbelievers and hypocrites.

Muhammad is Allah’s messenger, addressed as O Prophet, supported and forgiven by Allah. He receives commands to proclaim, fight, protect and safely convey seekers of protection, strive against disbelievers and hypocrites, take alms, pray for donors, and rely on Allah. He has pity for believers and is vexed by hypocrites.

The idolaters are addressed under treaty conditions and a proclamation of freedom from obligation. Some retain treaties; others who break pledges or attack religion are fought. They are excluded from the Inviolable Place of Worship, while protection-seekers are safeguarded and conveyed safely.

The believers repent, establish worship, pay the poor-due, obey Allah and Muhammad, and strive with their wealth and lives alongside the messenger. They praise, fast, bow, prostrate, enjoin right, forbid wrong, and keep Allah's limits, preferring Allah, His messenger, and striving over family and worldly possessions. From repentance and obedience through striving, they receive peace, mercy, acceptance, victory, promises of Gardens, the Garden, and supreme triumph.

The disbelievers oppose Allah’s guidance and obstruct His way. Though they seek to extinguish Allah’s light, their efforts fail; the Prophet strives against them harshly, and those rejecting Allah and His messenger face chastisement, humiliation, painful doom, and hell.

The hypocrites are a group of men and women marked by disbelief, doubt, false oaths, mockery, excuses, and avoidance of striving. They enjoin wrong, forbid right, withhold spending, and forget Allah. Opposed by the Prophet through striving and harshness, they are promised fire, lasting torment, punishment, and a painful doom in this world and the Hereafter.

l: the people of Medina, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: are_addressed_as believers The text does not mention the people of Medina by name.

l: the Last Day, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: is_believed_in_by the believers Belief in the Last Day is presented as a condition associated with tending Allah's sanctuaries and striving in His way. Those who believe in it are contrasted with those who do not.

l: the Greater Pilgrimage, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: has_a_day the day of the Greater Pilgrimage A proclamation from Allah and His messenger is made to all men on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage concerning freedom from obligation toward the idolaters.

l: the day of Huneyn, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: On the day of Huneyn, the believers' multitude avails them nothing, the earth becomes constricted for them, and they turn back in flight. Allah then sends reassurance to Muhammad and the believers, unseen hosts, and punishment upon those who disbelieved.

is_fulfilled_to the idolaters [until its term, when they remain faithful] Treaties with idolaters are to be honored when they remain true and do not support enemies. Those who break their pledges and attack the religion are subject to fighting, while faithful treaty-holders retain protection until their term.

Repentance is better than aversion and beneficial for idolaters and for those turning back from disbelief and hypocrisy. It accompanies worship and payment of the poor-due. Allah accepts it from His bondmen, may relent toward whom He wills, and may pardon mixed actions.

is_established_by the believers Establishing worship is required alongside repentance and payment of the poor-due for idolaters who seek freedom from fighting. Proper worship is also listed among the qualities of those who tend Allah's sanctuaries.

The poor-due is paid by believers and required of those who repent. Taken from wealth, it purifies and helps givers grow; the Prophet’s prayer reassures them. Allah accepts alms, distributed to the poor, needy, collectors, reconciled hearts, captives, debtors, Allah’s cause, and wayfarers.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: Revelations of Allah are traded for little gain, mocked by hypocrites, obstructed from His way, and met with Allah’s threat of disclosure.

l: the Religion of Truth, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: Allah sends Muhammad with guidance and the Religion of Truth so it prevails over all religion despite idolaters’ aversion.

l: the way of Allah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: is_striven_in the believers [with wealth and lives] The way of Allah is obstructed by some who seek worldly gain, while believers are commanded to strive in it with their wealth and lives. Contributions are also assigned for the cause of Allah.

l: the Inviolable Place of Worship, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: is_tended_by the believers [those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, observe worship, pay the poor-due, and fear none save Allah] The Inviolable Place of Worship is the site of a treaty with certain idolaters and is not to be approached by idolaters after the stated year. Tending it is not equal to believing in Allah and the Last Day and striving in Allah's way.

l: the Gardens of Eden, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: Gardens of Eden are promised blessed dwellings beneath flowing rivers where believing men and women abide forever; Allah’s acceptance is greater.

Hell is the promised ultimate abode of hypocrites, disbelievers, and wrongdoing people. It surrounds disbelievers and contains fire in which those who oppose Allah and His messenger abide, unfolding as the fate of rejection and opposition.

l: the sacred months, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: Four of twelve months are sacred by Allah’s ordinance; people must not wrong themselves, then the stated command concerning idolaters applies.

has_greater_reward_than the life of the world The Hereafter is presented as preferable to the life of the world, whose comfort is little in comparison. Believers are promised lasting reward there, while the works of disbelievers and hypocrites perish.

l: the life of the world, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: has_little_comfort comfort [compared with the Hereafter] The life of the world offers temporary enjoyment and little comfort compared with the Hereafter. Choosing worldly possessions, wealth, family, and dwellings over Allah, His messenger, and striving is condemned.

l: the migration from Mecca, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: is_described_as leaving homes [in Allah's way] The text does not mention the migration from Mecca by name.

l: the conquest at Huneyn, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: is_associated_with the day of Huneyn The text does not mention the conquest at Huneyn by name; it mentions the day of Huneyn, the believers' retreat, and Allah's subsequent support and victory.

l: the messenger of Allah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The messenger of Allah is followed and supported by believers, who strive alongside him; those preferring their own lives are condemned, while steadfast followers in hardship receive mercy.
are_pleasing_to Allah The Muhajirin who followed the messenger of Allah in the hour of hardship receive Allah's mercy. Allah is well pleased with them and has prepared the Garden for them.
are_pleasing_to Allah The Ansar who followed the messenger of Allah in the hour of hardship receive Allah's mercy. Allah is well pleased with them and has prepared the Garden for them.

l: the wandering Arabs, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: A group containing hypocrites, hardened disbelievers, the ignorant, and those resentful of spending, but also believers in Allah and the Last Day who will enter His mercy.

l: the townspeople of Al-Madinah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: include hypocrites [some persist in hypocrisy] Among the townspeople of Al-Madinah are people who persist in hypocrisy. Allah knows them, will chastise them twice, and will then relegate them to a painful doom.

has the townspeople of Al-Madinah Al-Madinah is the city whose townspeople include some who persist in hypocrisy. The townsfolk of Al-Madinah are not to stay behind the messenger of Allah and prefer their lives to his life.
The Garden, promised to believing strivers and early followers, is the supreme triumph: rivers flow beneath it, and those admitted abide there forever.

l: the mosque chosen to cause dissent, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The mosque chosen to cause dissent is founded on opposition and disbelief, meant to divide believers and aid those who warred against Allah and His messenger; the Prophet is commanded never to pray there.

l: the place of worship founded upon duty to Allah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: A place of worship founded upon duty to Allah from its first day is more worthy for prayer than one chosen to cause dissent; its men love purification, and Allah loves purifiers.
contains Allah's covenant Allah's covenant concerning the believers' lives and wealth is described as binding in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an.

A revealed surah commands belief in Allah and striving with His messenger; wealthy hypocrites seek to remain behind, while its revelation increases believers’ faith and increases wickedness in diseased hearts.

l: the revelation of a surah, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: causes hypocrites to turn away The revelation of a surah increases the faith of believers and causes them to rejoice. It increases wickedness in those whose hearts contain disease, and hypocrites turn away from it.

l: striving in Allah's way, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: brings the supreme triumph [for those who strive with wealth and lives] Striving in Allah's way is praised when believers use their wealth and lives. Thirst, toil, hunger, steps that anger disbelievers, spending, and crossing valleys are recorded as good deeds.

is an assuagement [for those for whom the Prophet prays] Prayer is not to be performed over a hypocrite who dies, and the Prophet is told not to pray for forgiveness for idolaters after their fate is clear. The Prophet is told to pray for those whose alms are taken.

is_a a cause of painful doom Disbelief is shown by rejecting Allah and His messenger, breaking Allah's word, and founding a place of worship in opposition and dissent. Those who persist in disbelief face punishment and hell.

is_broken_by hypocrites [through breaking their word and lying] Allah's covenant with believers is that He has bought their lives and wealth and that the Garden will be theirs. This promise is binding in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an.

Allah's mercy reaches the Prophet, the Muhajirin, the Ansar, and the three who were left behind after hardship. Allah may also show mercy to those who acknowledge their faults and mixed righteous action with bad action.

l: the supreme triumph, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The supreme triumph is promised to those who receive the Garden and to those who rejoice in the bargain of giving their lives and wealth for Allah's way.

l: the painful doom, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The painful doom afflicts disbelievers, hypocrites, liars, and wrongdoing people as the threatened reward for evil conduct in the world and the Hereafter.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The unit teaches that people will be brought back to Allah, Who knows the invisible and the visible, and will be told what they used to do. Hypocrisy is made a consequence in hearts until the day they meet Him.

l: the pledge of believers' lives and wealth, Surah 9: The Repentance (At-Tawba)
s: The pledge of believers' lives and wealth is Allah’s purchase of them for the Garden, recorded in the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an; believers fight, may slay and be slain, under Allah’s binding promise.

This unit concerns Allah’s revelation through Muhammad, the call to worship Allah, and the accountability of mankind after death. It contrasts believers, who receive guidance, mercy, good tidings, and the Garden, with disbelievers and wrongdoers, who face error, punishment, and the Fire. It recounts the experiences of Noah’s people, Moses, Pharaoh, the Children of Israel, and the folk of Jonah (Yunus) as signs of Allah’s power and judgment. The unit affirms creation and resurrection, the return to Allah, and the truth of the revelation.

Allah created the heavens and the earth, directs all things, and alone has authority over intercession, creation, resurrection, life, death, guidance, mercy, and judgment. He calls mankind to worship Him, promises the Garden to those who do good, and warns wrongdoers of the Fire and punishment.

Muhammad is commanded to warn mankind, recite the revelation, follow what is inspired to him, and worship Allah alone. He is told that he has no power to benefit or harm himself except as Allah wills and is not a warder over mankind.
Jonas (Yunus) is associated with a people who believed and thereby had the torment of disgrace removed from them and were given comfort for a while.

Moses was sent with Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Allah’s revelations. He challenged the magicians, called his people to trust Allah, prayed against Pharaoh and his chiefs, and was instructed to follow the straight path.

Pharaoh was a tyrant and a wanton who rejected Moses and Aaron and summoned magicians against them. He pursued the Children of Israel in rebellion and transgression, then professed belief when drowning overtook him, but his earlier rebellion was condemned and his body was saved as a portent.

Mankind is warned, tested, and held accountable for its conduct. People often turn to Allah in hardship and then rebel or become heedless after relief, while Allah does not wrong them and they wrong themselves.

Believers who do good works are guided by their faith and receive good tidings, mercy, peace, and the Gardens of Delight. They are promised security from fear and grief and good tidings in the life of the world and the Hereafter.
Disbelievers reject the revelations, call them magic, follow conjecture, and deny the meeting with Allah. They are threatened with boiling drink, painful doom, the Fire, and a dreadful punishment.
Messengers are sent to nations with clear proofs, and every nation has a messenger. On the Day of Judgment, judgment is made between each messenger and his people fairly, without wronging them.

The Children of Israel were brought across the sea and given a fixed abode and good things. They differed only after knowledge came to them, and Allah will judge between them concerning their disputes.
Egypt is the place where Moses and Aaron were sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and where Moses and his people were instructed to appoint houses as places of worship.
The earth contains signs of Allah and is provided with growth from water sent down from the sky. Its worldly adornment can be destroyed suddenly, and all that is in it belongs to Allah.
The heavens contain signs of Allah, and all that is in them belongs to Him. Nothing in the heavens, whether smaller or greater than an atom’s weight, escapes Allah’s knowledge.

The Qur'an is presented as a confirmation of what came before it and an exposition of what is decreed for mankind. It cannot be invented despite Allah, and those who claim it is invented are challenged to bring a surah like it.

The Garden is the home of those who do good works. Its people have rivers flowing beneath them, glorify Allah, exchange peace, praise the Lord of the Worlds, and abide there without dust or ignominy touching their faces.
The Fire is the home of those who earn ill-deeds and disbelieve. Its inhabitants abide there, with ignominy overtaking them and no protector from Allah.

The life of the world is temporary and is compared to vegetation that flourishes and is then made like reaped corn. It offers enjoyment and worldly provision, but its people ultimately return to Allah.
The Hereafter contains the return to Allah, judgment, reward, punishment, and the lasting outcomes of faith and deeds. Believers receive good tidings there, while wrongdoers face remorse and doom.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 10: Jonas (Yunus)
s: On the Day of Judgment, mankind and those who were treated as partners of Allah are gathered, distinctions are made, and every soul experiences what it did before. Nations are judged fairly, and no one is wronged.
Allah produces creation and then reproduces it so that believers may be rewarded with equity. He brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and all creation returns to Him.

l: the Flood and drowning of Pharaoh, Surah 10: Jonas (Yunus)
s: Noah and those with him were saved in the ship while those who denied Allah’s revelations were drowned. Pharaoh was later overtaken by drowning while pursuing the Children of Israel, and his body was preserved as a sign for those after him.

Revelation warns mankind, brings good tidings to believers, provides exhortation, healing for what is in the breasts, guidance, and mercy. Muhammad is commanded to recite it and follow what is inspired to him without altering it.
Faith is linked with belief in Allah, good works, trust in Him, and surrender to Him. Allah guides by faith, but no soul believes except by Allah’s permission.

Truth comes from Allah and is opposed to error, conjecture, invented claims, and magic accusations. Allah vindicates the truth by His words, and the truth is more deserving to be followed than what cannot guide itself.
Mankind is commanded to worship Allah and not call upon what cannot profit or hurt. The unit condemns assigning partners to Allah and describes worshippers who invoke others as following conjecture.
Allah leads to the truth and guides whom He wills to a straight path. Those who are guided benefit their own souls, while those who err harm only themselves.
